title: Search-Strategy Concept Map
subject: Artificial Computational Intelligence
targetAudience: Postgraduate students connecting uninformed and informed search, local search, and adversarial search into one mental map before exams.
summary: A cross-lecture concept map for Artificial Computational Intelligence that places every search strategy on a single map: uninformed (BFS, DFS, UCS, IDS), informed (greedy, A*), local (hill climbing, simulated annealing), and adversarial (minimax, alpha-beta, MCTS). It shows the I/O, the assumptions each strategy makes, how they compare, and the mistakes students make when picking one.
keyConcepts: Locate each search strategy on the axes of informedness, completeness, optimality, and space cost.
Connect heuristic design (Lecture 4) to A* admissibility and the trade-off with greedy search.
Relate local search to adversarial search through the idea of an evaluation function over a state space.
Avoid the classic mistakes: DFS on shallow-wide trees, greedy search that is incomplete, non-admissible heuristics breaking A* optimality.
